items.followUp: Explain why atomic size decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: An additional electron shell is added at each step down a group.
rubric.description: Identifies the increase in electron shells down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the number of electron shells increases or that each successive element has an additional shell.

rubric.why: The added shells place the outermost electrons farther from the nucleus, increasing atomic size.
rubric.description: Links the added shells to the increase in atomic size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus and that atomic size increases.

modelAnswer: Moving down a group, the number of electron shells increases; each successive element has an additional electron shell.
The outermost electrons are therefore farther from the nucleus, so atomic size increases.

items.followUp: Give two differences between ionic and covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Polar compounds have unequal charge distribution, whereas non-polar compounds have equal charge distribution.
rubric.description: Contrasts charge distribution in polar and non-polar compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting unequal and equal charge distribution or sharing.

rubric.why: Polar compounds have a net dipole moment; non-polar compounds have none.
rubric.description: Contrasts dipole moments in polar and non-polar compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the presence and absence of a net dipole moment.

modelAnswer: A polar compound has unequal charge distribution, whereas a non-polar compound has equal charge distribution.
A polar compound has a net dipole moment, whereas a non-polar compound has no net dipole moment.

rubric.why: Boiling point is defined as a temperature at which a specified change occurs.
rubric.description: Identifies boiling point as a temperature at which a change occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as the temperature at which the liquid changes state.

accept: liquid changes into a gas throughout the liquid
liquid changes into gas throughout the liquid
rubric.why: At the boiling point, a liquid changes into gas throughout the liquid.
rubric.description: States the change of state that occurs at the boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liquid changes into a gas at the boiling point.

modelAnswer: The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a gas throughout the liquid.

items.followUp: What is the solubility of a substance at a particular temperature?

rubric.why: Solubility refers to the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.description: Identifies solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that solubility is the maximum amount or quantity of solute.

rubric.why: The definition specifies the amount that dissolves in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature.
rubric.description: Includes the solvent mass, saturated solution, and temperature condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying 100 g of solvent, formation of a saturated solution, and a particular temperature.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in 100 g of a solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature.
